reviews.review_msg: I found the lectures and assignments engaging, although the course itself was challenging. The midterm and final were reasonably fair, but attending lectures and taking detailed notes on the case studies is essential for doing well
Good prof but the assignments were a nightmare
Easy course. Three assignments, one midterm and final. The final grade was generously curved.

Disagree with reviews. Class was fair. How can you complain about difficulty when midterm/final were multiple-choice quiz and 2-3 long questions. Skill issue lol. Prof scaled the grade too. Assignments had about a month before they were due. Class avg a B. Lectures recorded, didn't attend class once. Lightwork.
He curved the final grades quite generously and was really helpful throughout the course. The assignments are worth 30% and are quite easy.
Just received my grade. Average was below 50 percent.
Absolutely unfair finals and midterms.
The assignments were super confusing, the midterm and final average is very low. Would not recommend taking this course with him

kinda bad course I felt. Tao was like experimenting with us in the assignments with super confusing description and expectations - there was no clarity on it. Exams are like messed up. Just avoid taking this course with him.
beware of fake reviews posted by prof himself. Don't be fooled!
There are three assignments which were relatively easy but the midterm and finals were super hard with low class average
Hey Tao, stop posting fake positive reviews for yourself.

Chill professor, easy to listen to and the course was quite interesting. Medium workload with 3 assignments (30%) & 2 exams (70%). Sounds scary but the exams are fair in terms of difficulty/content (balance of hard & easy questions). Prof provides helpful mock exams and other resources. I'm happy I finished my degree with this class.

Prof made meaningful changes to the grading scheme to ensure that the new assignments are not screwing the students over. We were the guinea pigs for testing out some of the newer questions and we were given leniency on assignments and exams. I appreciate that we do not need to pass the exams to get a passing grade (C- or better). Overall not bad!
The assignments are so hard and no empathy for students. The midterm was mostly MCQS. Avg is very low. Don't take if you want to learn
It's mostly mcq, no effort to put QA, the grading is also not fair
Clear lectures, fair exams.

No empathy for students when they struggle, but themselves will fall behind schedule and mess up assignment due dates and make them due sooner than posted. As a student, I don't mind the prof making mistakes, we're all human. But the lack of compassion towards students, who likely have more going on in their life is just rude and inconsiderate.
Makes exam questions have answers based on a technicality. Makes assignments have acoustic clues that you need to decipher to figure out what he really wants.
Tao

Tao is very passionate and it's clear he's an expert, but he can come off as arrogant and looks down on students who are struggling. He also speaks fast and bases exams off of things he says, so it's difficult to keep up when you can't hear what he saying but it's important. He also seemed to get a kick off of people being upset over the midterm.

Pros: Accessible and responsive; good feedback if you ask.   
Cons (group project): too open-ended; groups poorly balanced; prompt was not good relative to other offerings; lectures were not helpful; not enough guidance; vague requirements.
Cons (exams): No practice questions; difficult; heavily based on lecture material. 
Bad learning experience

Pretty good lectures. Accessible outside of class. I don't get why people are complaining about implementing an AI! All that was asked was a simple, reasonably logical one for a board game you make! 
Midterm and Final questions were stuff mentioned in lectures and slides. 
Issue was that the material is mostly memorization based. Be prepared.

Never done so bad in course exams. Very memorization based and MCQ heavy but that's not a good thing. Project deadlines were quite late, as in you pretty much had to do 70% of the project in 2 weeks for the second deadline. It asks for an AI (way hard for a 200 course) as well. Pray for good group members or you're botched.

Prof Wang is an accommodating, kind professor. It is certainly hard to make group projects fair, nevertheless, the project with my group was fun, and I enjoyed doing it. However, the exam's MC are certainly difficult, as there are not much practice questions, and the questions cover many topics, making the testing scope broad I think

He also speaks fast and bases exams off of things he says, so it's difficult to keep up when you can't hear what he saying but it's important. Half of the course grade is on the project, which entails implementing AI in a 2nd year level course. If you find yourself with bad group members, you're done! It appears the professor doesn't address issues with unfavorable team assignments. It might be worth considering a different professor to save yourself some potential difficulties.

This is a rating for CMPT 276 with tao. it was his first time teaching the course and I can say this was one of the worst course experiences I've had. our course was 50% project based, and each phase of the project was revealed late, leading to short deadlines. the other 50% in exams was 2/3 mcq and was laid out poorly for the long answer.

He clearly cares, but I have to disagree about the "best CS lectures" review. His lectures are very rambly. He'll show a slide and just ramble about the topic in an unorganized way. He's not explaining the topic (teaching), he's just talking about it, as if he were having a conversation. It made his lectures unlistenable for me personally.

Tao has some of the best lectures in the CS department and is very good at keeping people engaged. However he needs to improve his course organization skills as we had an assignment due during finals. He also does not properly prep you for his brutal exams and aims to keep the avg low. That being said he is still better than most profs out there.
He did put a lot of effort into his slides and explained things well. Programming assignments are fun to do but does take a lot of effort. Good Prof in general.
lectures are engaging and course load is managable
